title: KPI handoff proxy: Prometheus/OTLP bridge and request fingerprinting for inference metrics
creator: Maya Rodriguez
description: Background: Our current Prometheus scraping and OTLP lane produce high-cardinality series for inference requests (prompt hashes, per-request ephemeral ids, unnormalized route labels) that drive up TSDB costs and make SLO calculations noisy. Goal: implement a lightweight KPI handoff proxy that sits between remote_write / OTLP producers and our ingestion fabric to perform schema-preserving label normalization, deterministic request fingerprinting, exemplar insertion linked to traces, and tenant-aware cardinality reduction before forwarding to the existing telemetry backbone. The proxy must support both Prometheus remote_write and OTLP gRPC input, enrich metrics with trace-context correlation headers (trace_id/span_id), and be configurable per-tenant to allow conservative / aggressive cardinality policies. It should be deployable as a small gateway in front of edge collectors and as a sidecar option for Dedicated nodes.
acceptance_criteria: A staging proxy is deployed and accepts Prometheus remote_write and OTLP gRPC traffic from the inference edge collector
Label normalization applies canonical mapping (route -> canonical_route, model -> model_family) and strips designated ephemeral keys (request_id, session_uuid) for forwarded series
Deterministic request fingerprint is computed per-request and added as a low-cardinality label (req_fingerprint) so metric rollups can attribute cost without exposing raw prompt text
Exemplars are injected for sampled latency/error events that include trace_id/span_id so traces and metrics are linked end-to-end
Cardinality reduction policy reduces unique timeseries in the test workload by >= 70% while preserving SLO-sensitive dimensions
End-to-end latency overhead introduced by the proxy is <3ms P95 for in-path enrichment on production-like traffic
Integration tests (unit + perf) and runbook for rollback are in place and documented in the design doc
A Grafana dashboard shows the difference in unique series count and a before/after SLO comparison for the canary cluster
notes: Trade-offs: we considered a heavy-weight centralized aggregator with persistent aggregation state but chose a stateless streaming proxy with bounded in-memory caches to keep failure blast radius small and scale independently
Decision: use deterministic hashing (XXH3) over prompt fingerprints + route to generate req_fingerprint; store only the hash and TTL to avoid PII leakage
Policy model: per-tenant config via ConfigMap for Dedicated and via ControlPlane ACL for hosted customers. Config includes keep_keys, drop_keys, sample_rate, cardinality_budget
Implementation detail: exemplars will be forwarded to the OTLP lane as OTLP.Exemplar attachments and to Prometheus as exemplar points when remote_write supports exemplars
Privacy: ensure all label scrubbing runs before any persistence; security review required for fingerprinting algorithm and TTL settings

test_plan:
- unit tests for label rewrite engine

notes_for_release: Feature gated behind feature flag 'kpi_handoff_proxy' and rollout plan: staging -> 2 canary clusters -> global. Monitor unique series, TSDB ingestion volume, and SLO regressions. Rollback: flip feature flag off and scale down to zero.
